test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The slant height of a right circular cone is 13 cm and the area of the base is 144π cm². Find the volume (in cm³) of the cone.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Radius**: Base area πr² = 144π ⇒ r = 12 cm.

Use the **Pythagorean Triplet** (5, 12, 13) where radius r = 12 and slant height l = 13.

∴ **Height (h)** of the cone = 5 cm.

**Volume** = (1/3) × Base Area × h = (1/3) × 144π × 5 = 48π × 5 = 240π cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 240π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Slant height (l)** = 13 cm

**Base Area** (πr²) = 144π cm²

**Formula Used:**

1. **Volume of cone** = (1/3) × πr²h

2. **Slant height relation**: l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfb3e1a30c2437513418e1fda8cdb24442a85c887eb40859c7aae89251672226.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base Area = πr² = 144π

⇒ r² = 144 ⇒ r = 12 cm

⇒ Using l² = r² + h²

⇒ 13² = 12² + h²

⇒ 169 = 144 + h²

⇒ h² = 169 − 144 = 25

⇒ h = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × 144π × 5

⇒ Volume = 48π × 5 = 240π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 240π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cone

The lateral or curved surface area is given by the formula CSA = π × r × l, where l is the slant height.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cone

The total surface area includes the base area and the CSA: TSA = πr(r + l).

Relation between Cone and Cylinder Volume

The volume of a cone is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height: V꜀ₒₙₑ = (1/3) × V꜀yₗᵢₙdₑᵣ.

Pythagorean Relation

In any right circular cone, the height (h), radius (r), and slant height (l) always satisfy l² = h² + r².</p
